content_record.title: Flavonoid from vine tea selectively clears senescent microglia, repairs DNA in aging cells
content_record.editorial_body: Dihydromyricetin, a natural flavonoid, acts as a senomorphic in fibroblasts by boosting PRDX2 nuclear translocation for DNA repair, and as a senolytic in microglia by disrupting mitochondrial function—offering a dual mechanism to combat age-related decline. Dihydromyricetin protects senescent fibroblasts from DNA damage and reduces SASP. It promotes PRDX2 nuclear translocation to facilitate DNA repair in senescent cells. In microglia with low PRDX2, it triggers apoptosis via mitochondrial impairment. This signal is based on The natural flavonoid dihydromyricetin targets senescent cells via PRDX2 and alleviates age-related diseases. from PubMed. Read the original report for full context.
